Name: CUMoreNpcMod
Summary: A BepInEx mod for Casualties: Unknown Demo that adds more NPCs to the game. NPCs are built on the game's native character system (cloned Experiment body), featuring full limb physics, animation, blood circulation, and combat.
Description:
Version: 0.7.4.0
Author: hmm1313133
Mod GUID: com.cu.morenpcmod

===========================================================
>>> EARLY PREVIEW - READ ME FIRST <<<
===========================================================

  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\

[b][size=4]  [color=#ff0000]This is an EARLY PREVIEW release (v0.7.4.0).[/color]

  - It is a work-in-progress build, NOT a finished product.
  - You WILL encounter bugs, glitches, and rough edges.
  - NPCs may get stuck, teleport weirdly, behave erratically,
    or have visual issues.
  - Performance may be inconsistent in complex terrain.
  - Save game compatibility between versions is NOT guaranteed.

  If you are looking for a polished experience, please wait for
  the stable release. Bug reports, feature ideas, and media/feedback are all welcome![/size][/b]

  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\  /!\

===========================================================
DESCRIPTION
===========================================================

A BepInEx mod for Casualties: Unknown Demo that adds more NPCs to the game.
NPCs are built on the game's native character system (cloned Experiment body),
featuring full limb physics, animation, blood circulation, and combat.

NPCs bleed, feel pain, go into shock, lose consciousness, get dismembered,
and die - exactly like the player character. There is no fake HP bar; every
wound you inflict goes through the game's real damage and circulation systems.

------------------------------------------------------------
NPC TYPES
------------------------------------------------------------

| NPC      | Key      | Faction  | Speed | Sense | Default | Role                        |
|-----------|-----------|----------|-------|-------|---------|------------------------------|
| Raider    | raider    | Hostile  | 4.5  | 35    | Yes    | Armed enemy, hunts you down  |
| Companion | companion | Friendly | 3.5  | 30    | Yes    | Follows and protects you    |

------------------------------------------------------------
RAIDER (Hostile)
------------------------------------------------------------

Armed enemies that spawn in the world and hunt you down.

- **Gun combat**: Fires 3-5 round bursts with realistic spread based on
  distance, target movement, and recoil. Not a hitscan turret - you can dodge,
  break line of sight, and flank.
- **Reload**: Reloads when the magazine runs dry (2.5s). Once spare magazines
  are exhausted, permanently switches to melee. You can hear them reload -
  that's your window to push.
- **Surrender**: When badly wounded, may drop their weapon and give up. Walk
  close and press E to search them for loot.
- **Tactical retreat**: Flees when critically injured, with retreat chance
  depending on how deep underground you are. Will also flee if out of ammo
  and outmatched.
- **Alert broadcast**: When one Raider spots you, nearby Raiders are alerted
  to your position. Engage quietly or prepare to fight multiple enemies.
- **Animal retaliation**: Will shoot hostile animals that enter their range.
- **Depth-scaled gear**: Weapons, helmets, and body armor improve with
  underground depth - surface Raiders carry makeshift pistols and helmets;
  deep Raiders wield rifles, riot helmets, and trauma rigs. They also carry
  bandages and medical supplies for self-treatment.

------------------------------------------------------------
COMPANION (Friendly)
------------------------------------------------------------

A friendly NPC that follows you and watches your back.

- **Command menu**: Hover over the Companion and press E to open the command
  menu: Follow / Hold Position / Rally / First-Aid / Give Item / Feed / Hug /
  Comfort / Release / Rename.
- **Battlefield first-aid**: Automatically detects when you're bleeding, in
  severe pain, or unconscious, and runs over to apply first-aid using real
  bandage mechanics - stops bleeding, relieves pain, heals bones, reduces
  dislocations. Now also handles splints and disinfectant. Consumes item
  condition just like the player would.
- **Self-treatment**: When out of combat, Companions (and Raiders) treat their
  own wounds - bandaging bleeding, splinting fractures, disinfecting
  infections, and saline infusion for blood loss. Uses items from their
  inventory. Interrupted immediately if attacked.
- **Self-defense**: Engages threats in melee range, or at range (18 tiles)
  if equipped with a gun. Falls back behind you when badly hurt.
  Companions hold fire if the player or another friendly NPC is in the line
  of fire.
- **Catch-up**: If you get too far ahead, the Companion sprints to catch up
  (1.6x speed). If you're way out of range and off-screen, it safely
  teleports nearby so you're never permanently separated.
- **Emotion system**: A dual-axis mood model (Mood: -100 to +100, Trauma: 0
  to 100) drives behavioral changes. The Companion has a companion aura (Mood
  slowly rises near you), feels lonely when far away, and reacts to events:
  witnessing you get hit, critically wounded, self-harming, or killed;
  completing first-aid; being fed/given items; being hugged; first kill.
  Mood tiers: Content / Calm / Anxious (shorter follow distance) / Breaking.
- **Crisis progression**: If Mood stays critically low (Breaking) for 60s,
  the Companion enters Crisis (crouching breakdown). If left unattended for
  300s, descends into Despair. Hugging or comforting interrupts the
  deterioration.
- **Self-harm intervention**: When you trigger a self-harm attempt, a living
  Companion within 25 tiles rushes to stop you (cancels the attempt, 180s
  cooldown). If no Companion is in range, the self-harm proceeds and the
  Companion suffers a severe Mood/Trauma hit from sensing it.
- **Mindwipe (Release)**: In Despair, you can choose "Release" from the
  command menu to let the Companion take mindwipe - a 1:1 recreation of the
  native WipeRoutine (last words -> convulsion -> sleep -> awakens as a
  hollow shell). Mood/Trauma are permanently locked to 0; all emotional
  behaviors are disabled; dialogue switches to "...". Players within 20
  tiles witness it and gain trauma. censorMood mode de-intensifies the
  scene (no ragdoll, gentle last words).
- **Custom naming**: Name your Companion via the "Rename" option in the
  command menu. Names persist across layer transitions (stored by CompanionId
  in a local JSON file, max 16 characters).
- **Affection**: Successful first-aid, feeding, and hugs build affection.
  High affection (50+) unlocks deeper last words and late-night heart-to-
  heart dialogue.

------------------------------------------------------------
COMBAT & DAMAGE
------------------------------------------------------------

NPCs use the exact same damage system as the player:

- Shoot them in the head for instant unconsciousness and brain damage.
- Shoot them in the body for internal bleeding and blood loss.
- Dismember their limbs - they can lose arms and legs.
- They bleed out, go into shock, lose blood pressure, and die from
  blood oxygen starvation.
- Armor reduces incoming damage; wearables take durability damage.
- Melee weapons and fists work too - blunt force causes pain, trauma,
  and bleeding.

Wound them badly enough and they'll try to flee or surrender. They're not
mindless target dummies - they react to being hurt.

------------------------------------------------------------
NPC HEALTH VIEW
------------------------------------------------------------

Hover over an NPC and press R (the wound-view key) to open their health
panel - the same WoundView the player uses. You can drag medicine onto
their limbs just like treating yourself: bandages, splints, disinfectant,
tourniquets, bullet extraction, bone reset, and more.

- Works on any living NPC within range (configurable, default 6m).
- Optional "Unconscious NPCs only" mode for a more deliberate feel.
- When hovering a viewable NPC, the tooltip shows the keybind hint.
- Sleep/workout buttons are hidden while viewing an NPC to prevent
  accidental self-actions.
- Auto-closes if the NPC dies, is destroyed, or moves out of range.
- In multiplayer (KrokMP), defers to KrokMP's own NPC health view for
  networked bodies.

You can also open an NPC's inventory: hover over a living NPC and press
Tab (the toggle-inventory key) to open their radial menu. This reuses the
game's native inventory system - slots, containers, batteries, equip/
unequip, drop, and merge all work exactly as they do on the player. The
NPC's body is temporarily swapped in for inventory operations only;
player movement, combat, and camera are unaffected. Single-player only.

Wound view fixes when inspecting NPCs:
- ECG/heart monitor now displays the viewed NPC's heart rate, not the
  player's.
- Amputation adrenaline is applied to the NPC being amputated, not the
  player.
- Heartbeat and monitor sounds only play for the viewed body, not all
  bodies in the scene.
- Limb hover highlights use the viewed body's limb state (e.g. a
  dismembered NPC limb is correctly unselectable).
- The player's diagnosed infection data no longer leaks into the NPC
  view.

------------------------------------------------------------
SKIN PACKS
------------------------------------------------------------

NPCs support custom appearance via community skin packs.

1. Download a skin pack (PNG files named after the game's experiment-series
  sprites, e.g. experimentHead.png, experimentUpTorso.png, etc.)
2. Place it in: BepInEx/plugins/CUMoreNpcMod/skinpacks/<SkinName>/
  (also supports .zip files and ChangeSkinMP's resources/ folder)
3. Launch the game. Skins are randomly assigned to NPCs at spawn.

Sprite alignment is automatic - pivot and pixels-per-unit are copied from
the original game sprites at runtime.

------------------------------------------------------------
NPC SAVE / LOAD
------------------------------------------------------------

Living NPCs are now saved when the game saves, and restored when you
continue. The game's native SaveSystem only persists the player - this mod
adds a companion save file (save.npcs.sv) that captures all living NPCs.

What is saved per NPC:
- Body and limb state: blood volume, pain, shock, blood pressure, blood
  oxygen, internal bleeding, brain health, fractures, dislocations,
  dismemberment - the full physiology snapshot.
- Equipment: held items, worn items, container contents, weapon ammo
  (magazine rounds, chamber, reserve magazines, out-of-ammo flag), item
  condition.
- Identity: skin, voice type, skills (STR/RES/INT).
- Companion data: affection, mood, trauma, mindwipe state, first-kill flag,
  custom name, hold/follow state.

On load:
- The world is re-generated (the game has no saved world seed), so saved
  coordinates are advisory. Companions land near their owner; other NPCs
  try their original position first, then fall back to a hidden spawn
  point nearby.
- Restored Raiders are counted toward ecology population; the ecology
  system only tops up the difference.
- Multiplayer (KrokMP): save/load is skipped entirely - the server
  authority handles NPC state.

------------------------------------------------------------
IN-GAME MENU (F3)
------------------------------------------------------------

Press F3 in-game to open the settings panel. Everything applies instantly,
no restart needed.

- **Global**: Toggle mod on/off, set feature mode, max concurrent NPCs
  (0-50), spawn check interval.
- **Spawn Counts**: World spawn and event spawn min/max.
- **NPC Types**: Toggle each NPC type, adjust spawn weight, min/max counts,
  spawn position (near player or at crosshair).
- **NPC Management**: Clear all NPCs, clear corpses only, or remove
  individual NPCs from a live list showing combat readiness and distance.
- **Other**: NPC-Player collision toggle, player damage to Companions
  toggle, NPC health view, unconscious-only, inventory view, max distance.
- **Ecology Status**: Real-time display of ecology phase, Raider target vs
  actual count, pending spawns, current layer, grace/maintenance timers.

------------------------------------------------------------
CONSOLE COMMANDS
------------------------------------------------------------

Open the game console with ` (backtick):

| Command                              | Description                                        |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| npcspawn                            | List all NPC types                                |
| npcspawn [type] [count] [position]  | Spawn NPCs (position: cursor/player/random/x,y)    |
| npcremove [type|all] [count]        | Remove NPCs (nearest first)                        |
| npclist                              | List all active NPCs                              |
| companionarmed [weapon] [mags] [pos] | Spawn a companion with a gun and reserve mags      |
| npcrename [name]                    | Rename your nearest companion                      |
| npcemotion <sub> [args]              | Companion emotion debug: mood/trauma/affection    |
|                                      |  set, or trigger: comfort/hug/crisis/despair/    |

------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIGURATION
------------------------------------------------------------

Config file: BepInEx/config/com.cu.morenpcmod.cfg

Key settings: EnableMod, FeatureMode (World/Event/Both/Off), MaxConcurrentNpcs,
WorldSpawn min/max, EventSpawn min/max, SpawnCheckInterval, NpcHealthView,
NpcHealthViewUnconsciousOnly, NpcInventoryView, NpcHealthViewMaxDistance,
NpcPlayerCollision, PlayerCompanionDamage,
CompatibilityMode (AutoSafe/ForceEnable/Disable for KrokMP), VerboseNpcLogs.

Per-NPC-type entries for Enabled, SpawnWeight, MinCount, MaxCount.

**JSON tuning** (BepInEx/config/CUMoreNpcMod.npcs.json): Override any NPC's
speed multiplier, reward scale, bleed resistance, pain resistance, brain
damage resistance, blood volume, and detection range at runtime.

------------------------------------------------------------
HOTKEYS
------------------------------------------------------------

| Key  | Action                          |
|------|---------------------------------|
| F3  | Open/close settings menu        |
| F10  | Toggle verbose logging          |
| E    | Interact with NPC              |
| R    | View NPC health menu (hover)    |
| Tab  | Open NPC inventory (hover)      |
| `    | Open console (game default)    |

------------------------------------------------------------
MULTIPLAYER (KrokMP)
------------------------------------------------------------

When KrokMP is detected, NPCs automatically sync to all clients. The server
(host or dedicated) is the sole authority for NPC spawning, health, and ecology
- clients only display server state. NPC damage, first-aid, and death are all
resolved server-side and broadcast to everyone.

Each player can have their own Companion - ownership is resolved via the
multiplayer player list, not just the local camera. Companions persist across
layer transitions: their state (affection, hold/follow, skin, skills, emotion
data, custom name) is snapshotted when the world regenerates and restored in
the new layer.

Console commands and menu changes only affect the local client.

===========================================================
REQUIREMENTS
===========================================================

- BepInEx 5.x
- Casualties: Unknown Demo
- .NET Framework 4.8
- Optional: KrokMP (for multiplayer NPC sync)

===========================================================
INSTALLATION
===========================================================

1. Install BepInEx 5.x if not already installed.
2. Download CUMoreNpcMod_v0.7.2.0.zip
3. Extract into BepInEx/plugins/CUMoreNpcMod/
  BepInEx/
  └── plugins/
      └── CUMoreNpcMod/
          ├── CUMoreNpcMod.dll
          ├── Lang/
          │  ├── EN.json
          │  └── zh_CN.json
          └── skinpacks/
              └── (place skin packs here)
4. Launch the game.

Supports in-game auto-update: check the top-left of the main menu for
update notifications.

===========================================================
BUG REPORTS
===========================================================

Please include your BepInEx/LogOutput.log file when reporting bugs.
Enable Debug > VerboseNpcLogs or press F10 in-game for detailed diagnostics.

v0.7.4.0 (2026-08-10)
---------------------
NPC trap awareness, animal combat, Companion equipment overhaul,
teleport reliability, and pathfinding/movement improvements.

- Trap awareness: NPCs detect and pathfind around traps (spikes, mines,
  bear traps, barbed wire, gun mines, turrets, sound cannons, sawblades,
  coils). Companions warn you with directional voice cues.
- Animal combat: NPCs proactively engage hostile animals (Wall Biters,

- Companion equipment: Companions now spawn with depth-scaled weapons,

  first. Auto-pickup fills containers too.
- Teleport reliability: Distance threshold raised (45->60) with 6s
  off-screen confirmation. Approach side locked to prevent cross-side
  appearance. Cooldown tuned for better recovery.
- Pathfinding & movement: NPCs handle low passages, jumping, wall
  climbing, and rope exits more reliably with fewer stuck states. Path
  recalculation is less aggressive during committed movement actions,
  reducing jitter.

v0.7.3.0 (2026-08-05)

Early-game balance pass and bug fixes.

  18->14). Skill depth bonus slowed (every 3 layers instead of 2).
- Ecology rebalance: Raider population targets and hard caps roughly halved
  across all difficulty presets; maintenance intervals increased.
- Hostile NPC loot: Raiders now keep their inventory on death - search
  their body for gear instead of it scattering on the ground.
- Gunshot fix: native ray no longer continues through to terrain after
  hitting an NPC in single-player.
- Heartbeat sound fix: NPC bodies no longer play the critical_loop heartbeat
  across the entire map.
- Removed F7/F8/F9 debug hotkeys (use console commands instead).

v0.7.2.0 (2026-08-02)

Companion gun combat, NPC self-treatment, and quality-of-life toggles.

  friendly NPC is in the line of fire. Follow distance widened to match.
- NPC self-treatment: Raiders and Companions now treat their own wounds

Pathfinding performance optimizations and bug fixes.

- Pathfinding: chase/teleport now warmup with direct movement before first

  early-exit landing search; long-distance budget gating.
- Kill credit: experience only awarded to the player who actually damaged
  the NPC (within 15s), not nearby bystanders.
- Skill isolation: cloned NPC bodies now get their own Skills object instead

- Attack side-effects: NPC gunfire/melee no longer triggers native

NPC Ecology system - server-authoritative match lifecycle, population

- Phase-based lifecycle: Seeding -> Landing Grace -> Exploring -> Layer

- Long-range recycling: Raiders that drift far from all players AND remain
  unobserved for a configured duration are silently removed, freeing
  population budget.
- Corpse management: oldest corpses auto-cleaned (max 6 retained).

- When the world regenerates (descending to a new layer), living Companions

IMPROVED
- World-ready detection now waits for world generation to complete and

v0.4.2.0 (2026-07-24)
---------------------
NPC pathfinding and teleport reliability improvements.

- Teleport validation: NPCs now verify an executable path exists from the

  to unreachable spots and getting stuck.
- Teleport no longer drops NPCs below the player's level, preventing
  appearances from directly underneath or through floors.
- Crouch-before-jump fix: NPCs crouching in low passages now stand up before

- Raised ground detection: NPCs recognize 1-2 block steps ahead and stand up
  to jump over them, rather than mistaking them for low ceilings and staying

- Failed edge disabling: when a pathfinding action (jump, wall climb, etc.)
  fails repeatedly, that specific path segment is temporarily disabled for 8

- NPC temperature normalized: NPCs maintain a fixed 37 C body temperature,

v0.4.1.0 (2026-07-23)

[color=#D4D4D8]Just an idea for a new custom container. Shout out to the Big Gs' that made this mod exist= "Iza Carlos and JimmyKing".
There is an annoying thing called "lack of space" for players that want to loot anything and everything. So why not have a container that could hold all of that?.[/color]

[b][color=#d4d4d8][size=4]How to install and play?=[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#D4D4D8]
1-Download the file and extract them somewhere.
2-there is an assets file and antigravbag.dll inside the extracted files. put these two in the plugin folder of the BepInEx. and enjoy.[/color]

[b][color=#d4d4d8][size=4]What's the real feature?=[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#D4D4D8]
Anti-Grav bag: A container with infinite capacity, but with drawbacks. (Should be balanced ofc).
1-Holds infinite items, even the heavy ones; but the encumbrance reduction is 100%.(basically all items inside the container weight double.
2-like the Grav bag, can use battery. This one can use large batteries. Using batteries sets the encumbrance reduction to 0%. (All items now weight normally). Obviously the container would violently explode without a charged battery.
3-It's craftable.[/color]

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]BepInEx and CUCoreLib.[/color][/size]

[color=#D4D4D8][size=4][b]How to configure?=[/b][/size]

There are some configurations that can be made.(there are also notes on top of each config setting).
1-After installing the mod and running it once, config file is created in the \BepInEx\Config\ folder.
2-The name of the config file should be "com.carlo.casualtiesunknown.antigravbag.cfg".
3-You can open the file with notepad++ or even notepad if you want.

[size=4][b]Want a different color/style for the Anti-Grav Bag?=[/b][/size]

1-There is "antigravbag.png" in the assets folder that the mod uses. I made it myself but the original one that the creators made are in the "antigravbagoriginal" folder. you can replace the file if you want.
2-If you just want a completely different one or another one that you created yourself, just replace the "antigravbag.png" with the one you have (names MUST match).[/color]

[size=4][b]Shout outs[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Special thanks again to Iza Carlos for the coding the mod and JimmyKing for helping them and creating the Original anti grav bag asset and CUCoreLib that mad everything work. This mod belongs to them, I only published it with their permission, and will remove it if they desire.[/color]

Name: Casualties Unknown's Kitchen
Summary: A mod that adds food items and liquids, crafting recipes and custom items that allow you to cook food.
Description:
A food based mod that adds a large amount of new fruit and vegetables that spawn naturally in layers, three unique cooking tools that allow you to cook on the fly along with some new recipes to craft filling and yummy food.

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
This mod uses Jimmyking's CUCoreLib for items and the plants that spawn in the layers and is required for this mod to work, you will need the latest .DLL version of CUCoreLib or the version this mod is currently built on (Nightly Build before V1.0.3: [url=https://github.com/jimmyking9999999/CUCoreLib/releases/tag/nightly]Release Nightly Build · jimmyking9999999/CUCoreLib[/url])
Take CUCoreLib .DLL file and this mod's .DLL and place it inside of the BepInEx Plugins folder, afterwards run the game and to test if the mod is running successfully try spawning in something from this mod like a apple tree (through the console "spawn appletree").

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
This mod aims to make each layer feel less barren by including a lot of new forgery in the form of fruit and vegetables and gives you the tools (food cooking items) to cook with them, additionally there are some new recipes that both allow you to craft items you couldn't craft before and craft some of the custom items in this mod.

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
CUCoreLib .DLL file is required for this mod, the latest Steam demo release of Casualties Unknown (which is V7 at the time of writing this).

[size=4][b]Shout outs/ People who have contributed to this mod[/b][/size]
Big thanks to Shooms for custom item ideas (such as the jams in this mod) and Mr.Pi for creating the sprites for the apple tree, apple, apple pie and oven. 
Massive thanks to Jimmyking which without the CUCoreLib I wouldn't have made this mod along with the various cooking items, fruit and veg and some recipe items. He also helped with the code of this mod.
Author: MrMaker875

Name: Iza's War Food
Summary: Adds a variety of drink mixes, and MRE rations. Preferably consume with water.
Description:
[size=5]Iza's War Food[/size]

Iza's War Food is a BepInEx 5 content plugin for Casualties Unknown that adds extra drink mix packets, mixed drinks, and military-style K-, C-, and D-rations.

The mod is meant as small variety-of-life content: more food crate finds, more trader variety and flavour choices to keep your expie happy.

[line]

[size=4]Requirements[/size]

Casualties Unknown Demo
BepInEx 5 for Unity Mono
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/341]CUCoreLib[/url]
Windows x64 game install

[line]

[size=4]Installation[/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install BepInEx 5 into the Casualties Unknown game folder.[/*]
[*]Install CUCoreLib if you do not already have it.[/*]
[*]Launch the game once so BepInEx creates its folders.[/*]
[*]Place IzasWarFood.dll into a folder inside:[/*]
[/list][code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\[/code]
For example:
[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\IzasWarFood\IzasWarFood.dll[/code]Launch the game once to generate the config file:
[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\config\com.carlo.casualtiesunknown.izaswarfood.cfg[/code]
[line]

[size=4]What It Adds[/size]

[size=4]Drink mix packets:[/size]
Instant coffee
Fruit punch
Grape
Lemon-lime
Orange
Lemonade
Orange-pineapple
Berry
Cocoa
Chocolate milk
Irish cream cappuccino
French vanilla cappuccino
Mocha cappuccino

[size=4]Rations:[/size]
K-ration cheese tortellini with marbled pound cake
K-ration beef ravioli with crackers and cheese spread
K-ration chili with beans and jalapeno cheese spread
K-ration mozzarella and spinach ravioli with corn chowder
C-ration hard biscuits
C-ration cookies
C-ration preserved beef
C-ration spaghetti (Meat and Tomato variants)
C-ration veggie hash
C-ration hashbrowns
D-ration compressed chocolate

[line]

[size=4]Gameplay Notes[/size]

Drink mix packets can be mixed with liquids that have water quality. One full packet can flavor up to 1000 ml worth of water quality, and partial mixing uses only part of the packet condition (at a rate of 10% = 100Ml).

The mixer prioritizes a valid liquid container in the player's main hand, so a full 1 L of water in your inventory is not automatically all turned into powder drink unless that is the container you are actively using.

Some packets can also be eaten dry. This is usually not a good idea, but it can give a small effect at the cost of thirst and other side effects.

Lemonade mix and chocolate milk mix can be made by boiling down the existing lemonade or chocolate milk liquids. Partial amounts work in 100 ml chunks.

Rations have multiple uses instead of being consumed all at once.

Rations are not craftable. They are found as loot, trader food, and scattered around during worldgen.

[line]

[size=4]Configuration[/size]

The generated config is intentionally small:

[code]General.Enabled
General.RegisterRecipes
General.RegisterRations[/code]
If you delete the config file, BepInEx will regenerate it on next launch with the current defaults.

[line]

[size=4]Console Testing[/size]

A spawn category is included for quick testing:
[code]spawncategory izaswarfood[/code]This spawns the current drink mix packets and ration items in zero gravity.

[line]

[size=4]Compatibility[/size]

This mod is additive. It registers new items, liquids, recipes, locale entries, and a small spawncategory helper.
It may conflict with other mods that heavily replace item registration, recipe crafting, liquid behavior, or console spawn categories.
Mods that only add unrelated items, UI, audio, or quality-of-life behavior are more likely to be fine.

[line]

[size=4]Save and Uninstall Notes[/size]

The plugin does not intentionally write custom persistent save data.
Because this mod adds custom item and liquid IDs, removing it during a run may leave missing references if your current save contains its items or liquids.
For safest uninstalling, finish or abandon the current run first, then remove:
[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\IzasWarFood\[/code]Optional:
[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\config\com.carlo.casualtiesunknown.izaswarfood.cfg[/code]
[line]

[size=4]Troubleshooting[/size]

If the items do not appear:
[list]
[*]Confirm BepInEx 5 loads.[/*]
[*]Confirm CUCoreLib is installed and loading.[/*]
[*]Confirm IzasWarFood.dll is inside BepInEx\plugins.[/*]
[*]Launch once and check that the config file was generated.[/*]
[*]Check that General.Enabled is true.[/*]
[*]Use spawncategory izaswarfood to confirm the plugin is active.[/*]
[/list]
If recipes do not appear:
[list]
[*]Check that General.RegisterRecipes is true.[/*]
[*]Check the Food crafting category.[/*]
[/list]
If rations do not appear:
[list]
[*]Check that General.RegisterRations is true.[/*]
[*]Use spawncategory izaswarfood to confirm they registered.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=4]Credits[/size]
[list]
[*]Built with BepInEx 5.[/*]
[*]jimmyking9999999 for CUCoreLib.[/*]
[*]TheTeaChugger for the idea[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=4]Version[/size]

Current workspace version: 1.0.0

This build is experimental and may change as the underlying game and mod hooks are better understood.

[*]BepInEx[/*]
[*]KrokMP（必需）[/*]

[/list]Shout outs
感谢 Casualties Unknown 原作与社区；感谢 KrokMP 提供联机基础；感谢测试与反馈的玩家们:WC567765。

Burn Care (烧伤护理) — Installation
===================================

This is the standalone Burn Care mod .

Burn Care requires KrokMP (Casualties: Together). Without it the mod
will not load. Recommended: install KrokMP, then Burn Care, then
host your own room (solo hosting is fine).


Requirements
------------
  • Casualties Unknown (matching build)
  • BepInEx 5.x
  • KrokMP (required — hard dependency)


Install
-------
1. Close the game.

2. Open the game folder:
    Steam → right-click the game → Manage → Browse local files

3. Install BepInEx if missing, then install KrokMP from its own release
  (follow that package’s INSTALLATION.txt).
  You should have:  BepInEx\plugins\KrokMP\

4. Create a folder for this mod, for example:
    BepInEx\plugins\BurnCare\

5. Put into that folder:
    BurnCare.dll
  Optional Chinese UI patch (if included):
    BurnCareZhPatch.dll
    Locale\  (if the release ships a Locale folder, keep it next to the DLL)

6. Do NOT put Burn Care files inside KrokMP\.
  Keep them as a separate folder under plugins\.

7. Launch from Steam → open multiplayer → host your own room → play.


If it fails
-----------
Check BepInEx\LogOutput.log for “BurnCare” / missing KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.

Name: Makeshift Prosthetics
Summary: Adds functional improvised prosthetics, mechanical durability, repairs, environmental wear, progressive Twisted and Mangled injuries, traumatic amputations, head prosthetics,harder starter scenarios and extensive balance settings to Casualties Unknown.
Description:
[center][size=6][b]MAKESHIFT PROSTHETICS![/b][/size]

[size=4]Losing a limb is no longer the end of your run.[/size]
[i]But there will be price to be paid in order to survive.[/i]
[/center]

[line]

[size=5][b]ABOUT THE MOD[/b][/size]

Makeshift Prosthetics turns limb loss into a complete survival system for Casualties Unknown.

Instead of simply accepting a missing limb, you can build or find an improvised replacement and return your character to action. That replacement will not behave like an organic body part.

A wooden hook cannot perform precise work. A cable-driven arm contains mechanisms vulnerable to damage and moisture. A peg leg may keep you moving, but it will never provide the comfort or mobility of a healthy leg. Every prosthetic restores something while introducing a new limitation.

The mod also expands organic trauma. Limbs can become permanently Twisted, deteriorate into Mangled states, develop recurring infections, and eventually be lost through traumatic amputation.

[b]This is a gameplay and injury overhaul, not a cosmetic limb pack or an “upgrade me into a supersoldier, daddy~” mod.[/b]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784989759-1055977088.png[/img][/center]
[line]

[size=5][b]MOD PHILOSOPHY[/b][/size]

Makeshift Prosthetics is not intended to turn limb loss into a direct upgrade.

Its replacements are designed to compensate for injury rather than outperform a healthy organic body. Even advanced prosthetics restore only part of the lost function and introduce their own restrictions, maintenance requirements, and environmental weaknesses.

[b]The goal is to let a badly injured character keep surviving, not to make voluntary amputation the strongest path.[/b]

[line]

[size=5][b]WHAT THE MOD ADDS[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Functional arm and leg prosthetics with different capabilities and limitations[/*]
[*]Separate Casing and Mechanics condition for artificial limbs[/*]
[*]Field repairs using construction-specific materials[/*]
[*]Powered prosthetics with replaceable batteries and water-short mechanics[/*]
[*]Water, liquid, dirt and use-related mechanical wear[/*]
[*]Grip, crafting, tool and medical-minigame restrictions[/*]
[*]A functional Wooden Jaw, Eye Bandage and Veteran Eye Patch[/*]
[*]Permanent Twisted and Mangled organic injuries[/*]
[*]Traumatic amputations caused by severe injuries[/*]
[*]Hatred of Flesh and low-morale self-amputation incidents[/*]
[*]Alternative starting scenarios[/*]
[*]Optional integration with the Prosthetics mod[/*]
[*]Multiplayer support through KrokMP[/*]
[*]Extensive balance, visual and accessibility settings[/*]
[/list][line]

[color=#C99562][size=5][b]CRUDE AND WOODEN PROSTHETICS[/b][/size][/color]

Early prosthetics are cheap enough to save a desperate survivor, but their functionality is limited.

[size=4][b]Crude Hook[/b][/size]

A simple replacement for a missing hand.

[list]
[*]Restores basic hand functionality[/*]
[*]Can hold selected items suitable for a hook[/*]
[*]Can substitute for a cutting tool in compatible crafting[/*]
[*]Cannot use firearms, lockpicking equipment or precision tools[/*]
[*]Restricts applicable medical actions[/*]
[*]Can catch against walls during a normal wall slide[/*]
[/list]Wall sliding gradually damages the hook. If you keep doing it with a nearly destroyed one, it can eventually break completely.

[size=4][b]Makeshift Gripper[/b][/size]

A mechanical hand and forearm with a crude gripping mechanism.

[list]
[*]Can hold far more items than the Crude Hook[/*]
[*]Can perform a wider selection of medical actions[/*]
[*]Still cannot reproduce precise finger movement[/*]
[*]Cannot properly use firearms, lockpicking equipment and selected precision tools[/*]
[*]Can substitute for a simple Hammering tool in compatible crafting[/*]
[*]Requires battery power for full functionality[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Wooden Foot, Crude Peg Leg and Makeshift Full Leg[/b][/size]

Primitive replacements for different levels of leg loss.

The Wooden Foot replaces only the foot. The Crude Peg Leg replaces the lower leg and foot. The Makeshift Full Leg replaces the entire missing leg.

All of them restore mobility far beyond what an amputated character would otherwise have, but remain less effective and less stable than a healthy organic leg.

The Makeshift Full Leg is powered and requires battery charge for full functionality.

[center]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784989782-1511256080.png[/img]
[/center]
[line]


[color=#8FA8C9][size=5][b]CABLE-DRIVEN PROSTHETICS[/b][/size][/color]

Cable Arm and Cable Leg are more advanced replacements built around powered mechanical systems.

They restore substantially more functionality than primitive prosthetics, but require batteries and contain vulnerable internal mechanisms.

[list]
[*]Restore most ordinary limb functionality[/*]
[*]Require advanced materials and higher Intelligence to craft[/*]
[*]Use replaceable batteries[/*]
[*]Lose much of their effectiveness when discharged[/*]
[*]Are especially vulnerable to moisture and direct liquid exposure[/*]
[*]Can short circuit when badly damaged and wet[/*]
[/list]The [b]Veteran Cable Hook-Hand[/b] is a specialized Cable Arm rebuilt around a Thornback Elder Fang.

The fang can only be obtained by killing that greedy bitchass in melee combat.

Veteran Hook sacrifices normal grip functionality for mobility, cutting utility and stronger attacks. It greatly assists wall sliding and repeated wall jumps.

Wall use can still damage the Veteran Hook normally, but does not cause permanent maximum-condition loss.

Press [b]H[/b] by default to open the battery panel for a compatible installed or held prosthetic.

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990259-1621931850.png[/img][/center]
[line]

[size=5][b]MECHANICAL BODY PARTS[/b][/size]

Artificial limbs are treated as machinery rather than organic flesh.

They do not bleed, biologically heal, develop normal organic infections, suffer hypoxemia, fractures or dislocations, and ordinary medicine cannot magically regenerate them.

Every prosthetic segment uses two separate condition layers:

[list]
[*][b]Casing — Skin Health[/b]: external shell, frame and structural protection[/*]
[*][b]Mechanics — Muscle Health[/b]: joints, cables, wiring and internal functionality[/*]
[/list]A prosthetic can have an intact shell while its internals are barely functional. Likewise, a working mechanism can remain inside a casing that is about to fall apart.

Both layers must be maintained separately.

If a prosthetic is completely destroyed, it may leave behind 1–2 pieces of material from its construction.

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990514-480776208.png[/img][/center]
[line]

[size=5][b]FIELD REPAIRS AND ENVIRONMENTAL WEAR[/b][/size]

Installed prosthetics can be repaired directly through the health panel without removing them.

Different constructions accept different materials, including:

[list]
[*]Wood panels and cubes[/*]
[*]Metal panels and cubes[/*]
[*]Scrap metal[/*]
[*]Rope[/*]
[*]Circuit boards[/*]
[*]Wire bundles[/*]
[/list]Casing and Mechanics are repaired separately.

Improvised machinery is also affected by the environment:

[list]
[*]General wetness gradually damages internal mechanics[/*]
[*]Direct liquid contact causes significantly stronger wear[/*]
[*]Dirt and heavy contamination damage moving parts[/*]
[*]Circuit-heavy prosthetics are especially vulnerable to moisture[/*]
[/list]A badly damaged powered prosthetic may short circuit in water, causing pain, shock and battery drain.

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990314-1088998042.png[/img][/center]
[line]

[color=#C45B5B][size=5][b]PERMANENT ORGANIC TRAUMA[/b][/size][/color]

Makeshift Prosthetics adds lasting outcomes between an ordinary injury and complete limb loss.

[size=4][b]Twisted[/b][/size]

A Twisted limb is permanently damaged but still usable.

Fractures and dislocations may begin its development. After the original injury is treated, the limb gradually develops reduced Health caps and slower medical performance.

Additional serious trauma can begin deterioration toward Mangled.

Twisted penalties also affect connected lower segments:

[list]
[*]Upper Arm > Forearm > Hand[/*]
[*]Thigh > Crus > Foot[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Mangled[/b][/size]

A Mangled limb has suffered catastrophic and effectively permanent destruction.

It retains almost no mechanical function, has heavily reduced Health caps, performs medical actions poorly, and develops recurring infection.

Possible causes include explosions, massive single-hit damage, complete muscular destruction, and finished deterioration of a Twisted limb.

Mangled destruction spreads gradually through lower connected segments rather than applying instantly.

[size=4][b]Traumatic Amputation[/b][/size]

A sufficiently severe new injury may physically remove a limb without first creating Mangled.

Normal limbs have a relatively low risk. Twisted, deteriorating, and Mangled limbs become progressively more vulnerable to fractures, explosions, heavy collisions, and critical damage.

All major chances, thresholds, and progression times can be adjusted in the mod settings.
[center][/center]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784989971-799861114.png[/img]

[line]

[color=#B78BC7][size=5][b]HEAD PROSTHETICS AND ACCESSORIES[/b][/size][/color]

[size=4][b]Crude Wooden Jaw[/b][/size]

The Wooden Jaw restores the mouth after complete jaw loss.

It allows limited speech, eating and mouth-based item handling, but does not fully reproduce an organic jaw.

Speech remains impaired, eating is less effective and the prosthesis has its own visual and status handling.

[size=4][b]Eye Bandage[/b][/size]

Simple field dressing for a damaged or missing eye.

Makes you a pirate.

Kekw.

It provides basic protection and covers the damaged socket, but has none of the Veteran Eye Patch's special danger-sense abilities.

[size=4][b]Veteran Eye Patch[/b][/size]

A reinforced eye covering that can only be equipped after losing an eye.

The patch provides minor head protection and has a [b]75% chance[/b] to absorb an otherwise destructive injury to the remaining eye at the cost of its own condition.

It also provides an instinctive danger-sense ability capable of detecting traps, mines, turrets, Sound Cannons, hostile creatures and several environmental threats.

Visible and blind areas use different warning effects, while active threats receive stronger indicators.

Default detection range:

[b]One eye missing — 20 tiles[/b]
[b]Both eyes missing — 40 tiles[/b]

A Reduced Flashing option is available.
[center][left]
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990075-164037306.png[/img][img width=302]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990088-481996230.png[/img][/center]
[/left]
[/center]

[line]

[size=5][b]HATRED OF FLESH[/b][/size]

Hatred of Flesh is an optional permanent psychological condition built around rejection of the character's organic body.

Remaining organic limbs restrict maximum mood.

As more flesh is lost and replaced, the penalty gradually weakens while control over prosthetics improves. Extensive artificial replacement can also provide resistance to damage received by Makeshift prosthetics.

The condition includes:

[list]
[*]A unique moodle with dynamic information[/*]
[*]Mood penalties based on remaining organic body parts[/*]
[*]Increasing prosthetic efficiency as more flesh is lost[/*]
[*]Prosthetic damage resistance at high replacement levels[/*]
[*]Unique character dialogue and critical episodes[/*]
[*]A chance of self-amputation during severe incidents[/*]
[/list]Hatred of Flesh can be disabled completely in the run settings.

[center][i][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990171-875354083.png[/img][/i][/center]
[line]

[size=5][b]STARTING SCENARIOS[/b][/size]

The mod includes optional starts built around catastrophic injury.

[list]
[*][b]Broken Capsule Survivor[/b] — begin severely wounded after a disastrous arrival and rebuild yourself with whatever can be found[/*]
[*][b]Pirate[/b] — begin with several missing body parts and crude replacements[/*]
[*][b]Hatred of Flesh[/b] — begin with the psychological condition already active[/*]
[/list]These scenarios are intended to demonstrate the mod's systems and provide difficult alternative starts, not easy bonus loadouts.

[center][i][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/8391/images/460/460-1784990202-173430493.png[/img][/i][/center]

[line]

[size=5][b]OTHER DETAILS[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]DRAUGHT OF HORRIBLE AGONY[/b][/size]

A deliberately horrible crafted liquid that can be applied directly to an arm or leg to remove it.

The process is slow, extremely painful and damages nearby connected tissue before the limb is finally severed.

Applying it to the head does not decapitate the character. Instead it destroys the eyes, relevant dressings and head equipment, the jaw, and leaves the head severely damaged.

Drinking it is totally safe and may give you superpowers like Neurobooster.

The liquid can also rarely appear inside generated mini barrels.

[size=4][b]TRADER REACTIONS[/b][/size]

Traders notice extensive prosthetic replacement and may comment on the character's condition through unique conversations and player responses.

Dune has his own prosthetic interaction.

If he attempts to bite an artificial limb, the prosthetic casing is damaged instead of organic flesh, his teeth hurt, and reputation suffers accordingly.

M-metal... not tasty...

[size=4][b]SMALLER INTEGRATIONS[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Prosthetics use dedicated installation, removal, repair and break feedback. Use a wrench to remove installed limb prosthetics[/*]
[*]Destroyed prosthetics can leave behind useful construction scraps[/*]
[*]Debug tools and console commands are included for repair, integrity checks and trauma testing[/*]
[*]Most optional mechanics can be disabled or heavily rebalanced without removing the core prosthetic system[/*]
[*]Very low mood can develop into a complete mini-event involving warnings, dialogue, self-amputation and permanent consequences[/*]
[*]Unique character phrases and reactions exist for most major mechanics of the mod[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]CONFIGURATION[/b][/size]

Most major systems can be adjusted through the Makeshift Prosthetics settings panel.

Configurable values include:

[list]
[*]Twisted, Mangled and traumatic-amputation chances[/*]
[*]Critical trauma thresholds and development timers[/*]
[*]Organic Health caps and minigame penalties[/*]
[*]Prosthetic Casing and Mechanics damage[/*]
[*]Permanent prosthetic wear[/*]
[*]Environmental damage and moisture sensitivity[/*]
[*]Repair effectiveness[/*]
[*]Battery drain and water-short behavior[/*]
[*]Grip and medical-action restrictions[/*]
[*]Eye Patch danger-sense behavior[/*]
[*]Hatred of Flesh and self-amputation[/*]
[*]Starting scenarios[/*]
[/list]Most gameplay systems can be weakened, disabled or heavily rebalanced.

Diagnostic options, compatibility overrides and experimental ProstheticsBridge features are kept separately under the DEBUG section.
[line]

[size=5][b]EXPERIMENTAL FEATURES[/b][/size]

The following WIP systems are included but disabled by default:

[list]
[*][b]Damaged cable prosthetic water shock[/b] — heavily damaged cable limbs may discharge when exposed to water
[/*]
[/list]Experimental systems may change significantly between releases or become normal feature after a while.

[line]

[size=5][b]INSTALLATION[/b][/size]

Extract the archive into:

[code]
Casualties Unknown/BepInEx/plugins/[/code]The final structure should look like this:

[code]
Casualties Unknown/
└── BepInEx/
    └── plugins/
        └── MakeshiftProsthetics/
            ├── MakeshiftProsthetics.dll
            └── Assets/[/code][b]Do not separate the DLL from its Assets folder.[/b]

[line]
[b][size=5]REQUIREMENTS[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]BepInEx 5.4[/*]
[*]CUCoreLib[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=5][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/40]PROSTHETICS[/url] MOD INTEGRATION[/b][/size]

When installed, [b]ProstheticsBridge[/b] connects both mods into the same anatomy and progression system.

[list]
[*]Makeshift and Prosthetics limbs cannot occupy the same body chain at once[/*]
[*]Wooden Jaw and Copper Jaw are mutually exclusive[/*]
[*]Prosthetic Eyes are recognized by the Eye Patch system[/*]
[*]External prosthetics interact with Hatred of Flesh, dialogue and trader reactions[/*]
[*]Cable Arm can support one Prosthetics shoulder augment slot[/*]
[/list][b]Balanced Compatibility[/b] is enabled by default.

Prosthetics loot begins appearing only after five completed layers, then gains [b]2.5% appearance chance per additional cleared layer[/b].

Balanced mode allows selected advanced content such as Titanium limbs, Prosthetic Eyes and Copper Jaw while restricting most powerful augments, crates, neuromods and similar progression-skipping content.

Titanium limbs and Copper Jaw can be found, but are not craftable or trader stock in Balanced mode.

A [b]Soft Compatibility[/b] switch is available under DEBUG for players who want the normal Prosthetics ruleset without Makeshift's progression restrictions.

[line]

[size=5][b]SUPPORTED MODS[/b][/size]

Makeshift Prosthetics includes dedicated compatibility handling for several community mods.

None of them are required for the core mod. If they are installed, Makeshift detects them automatically and tries very hard not to let two completely different medical systems fight over the same leg.

[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/40][b]Prosthetics[/b][/url]

Largest integration. Look above if you forgot how comp works.
[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/7][b]QoL Unknown[/b][/url]

General quality-of-life improvements that fit naturally beside Makeshift. Makeshift includes compatibility for QoL save slots, prosthetic-safe healing and overlapping Sound Cannon indicators. Recommended even if you do not care about any of the larger medical overhauls.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/452][b]Alexx_'s Medical Brutalism[/b][/url]

Adds a harsher collection of organic injuries, diseases and medical effects. Makeshift protects artificial limbs from Brutalism effects that are intended for flesh, including incompatible wounds and organic regeneration. Good choice if your opinion on surviving catastrophic injury is that the game should punish you even harder.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/440][b]NeurotraumaModik[/b][/url]

A deeper medical overhaul focused on surgery, necrosis, organ damage and long-term complications. Makeshift artificial segments are recognized as prosthetics and excluded from incompatible organic limb conditions and procedures.[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]MULTIPLAYER[/b][/size]

Multiplayer is supported through [b]KrokMP[/b].

KrokMP is optional and is [b]not required for single-player[/b].

Makeshift synchronizes installed prosthetics, body changes, starting scenarios, batteries, breakage, persistent trauma states and relevant ProstheticsBridge interactions.

For multiplayer, all players should use the same versions of Makeshift Prosthetics and other gameplay-changing mods.

As always with modded multiplayer: if you create some cursed mod combination nobody has tested before, God is your only technical support.

[line]

[size=5][b]BETA WARNING[/b][/size]

[b]Makeshift Prosthetics is in active development.[/b]

Features, recipes, balance values, visuals, save data, and internal systems may change between releases.

Back up important saves before installing a new beta version. Experimental features are disabled by default and may behave unpredictably when enabled.

Feedback and detailed bug reports are welcome.

[line]

A replacement can return a character to action, but every improvised solution brings new weaknesses: limited grip, reduced precision, mechanical wear, difficult maintenance, and permanent consequences from the injury that made it necessary.

Name: Random Events
Summary: Feel like your game is missing a bit of action? Spice up your multiplayer lobbies with random item drops, enemy spawns, and more!
Description:
[b][color=#d4d4d8][size=4]Random Events[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#D4D4D8]A randomizer mod for Casualties Unknown multiplayer. While you host a world, every so often it rolls a weighted-random event and announces it in chat: giving items to everyone, spawning traps and enemies, triggering earthquakes/radline, and running host moderation actions on a random player. Everything is driven by an editable config, so you decide what can happen and how often.

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size][/color]

[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8][b]KrokMP[/b] - required. RandomEvents only runs while you host a multiplayer world and stays idle without it.[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8][b]CatPatch[/b] - optional. Enables the moderation category (revive/kill/knockout/fling/etc.). When it's not installed, that category is skipped automatically.[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8][b]Cheats enabled[/b] on the host.[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8]Only the [b]host[/b] needs RandomEvents. Other players just need KrokMP; effects replicate to them.[/color][/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[size=4][b]Install[/b][/size]
1. Install BepInEx and KrokMP first.
2. Extract this archive into your game folder so you get: [/color][color=#d4d4d8]BepInEx/plugins/RandomEvents/RandomEvents.dl[/color][color=#D4D4D8] and [/color][color=#d4d4d8]BepInEx/config/randomevents.cfg[/color][color=#D4D4D8].
3. Launch the game and host a world.

[b][size=4]Usage[/size][/b][/color]
[color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8]Open the dev console and type [/color][/color][color=#d4d4d8]re[/color][color=#D4D4D8][color=#D4D4D8]:[/color][/color]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re on[/color][color=#D4D4D8] / [/color][color=#d4d4d8]re off[/color][color=#D4D4D8] / [/color][color=#d4d4d8]re toggle[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - enable/disable[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re interval <seconds>[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - time between events[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re roll[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - fire one now[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re reload[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - reload the config after editing[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re update[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - check for a new version (if configured)[/color][/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][color=#d4d4d8]re status[/color][color=#D4D4D8] - current settings and detected mods[/color][/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
[b][size=4]Config[/size][/b]
Edit [/color][color=#d4d4d8]BepInEx/config/randomevents.cfg[/color][color=#D4D4D8], then [/color][color=#d4d4d8]re reload[/color][color=#D4D4D8]. Each entry has a weight, a command, and optional announce lines (one is picked at random). Categories and entries can be gated to installed mods with [/color][color=#d4d4d8]requires=[/color][color=#D4D4D8] (e.g. [/color][color=#d4d4d8]requires=catpatch[/color][color=#D4D4D8]). See the comments at the top of the file.

[b][size=4]Updates[/size][/b]
RandomEvents automatically checks for new updates and will notify you if a newer version is available. You will be able to download the update directly and use it on game restart.[/color]

[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[b][color=#D4D4D8]BepInEx must be installed first.[/color][/b]

Make sure the order is:

Place replacement sprites here!                 \Casualties Unknown Demo\BepInEx\plugins\SkinDeep\Sprites

[b]Experiment_Limb_#_Outline.png[/b]

Name: Casualties Supercharged
Summary: Adds a chance of spawning more powerful version of (most) traps ingame that deal more damage in general. Semi-unbalanced.
Description:
[size=5]Casualties: Supercharged[/size]

[quote][color=#f4cccc]This mod contains extremely loud sounds, mainly "sonarmegaouch.ogg". If you are sensitive to loud sounds i recommend you turn on UseLightHitSound in config.[/color][/quote][line]

Casualties: Supercharged is a BepInEx 5 plugin for Casualties Unknown that adds configurable supercharged versions of vanilla traps.

Supercharged traps are still based on the original game traps, but they can roll into stronger variants during world generation, use optional custom sprites and sounds, and apply harsher or stronger effects. Making certain trap encounters feel like rare, nasty outliers.

It is worth noting that supercharged traps may feel unfair, if so feel free to adjust the associated config.
[line]

[size=4]Requirements[/size]

Casualties Unknown Demo
BepInEx 5 for Unity Mono
Windows x64 game install
[line]

[size=4]Installation[/size]

Install BepInEx 5 into the Casualties Unknown game folder.

Launch the game once so BepInEx creates its folders.

Place CasualtiesSupercharged.dll into a folder inside:

[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\[/code]
If the release includes an Assets folder, keep it next to the DLL, for example:

[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\CasualtiesSupercharged\CasualtiesSupercharged.dll
<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\CasualtiesSupercharged\Assets\SuperchargedTraps\[/code]
Launch the game once to generate the config file:

[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\config\com.carlo.casualtiesunknown.superchargedtraps.cfg[/code]
Edit the config if you want different spawn chances, damage values, cooldowns, charge times, or screen effect strength.

[line]

[size=4]What It Does[/size]

Adds supercharged variants for:

[list]
[*]Landmine[/*]
[*]Gunmine[/*]
[*]Turret[/*]
[*]Sound cannon[/*]
[*]Launch pad[/*]
[*]Spike stabber[/*]
[*]Bear trap[/*]
[*]Coil[/*]
[/list]
World generation can replace supported vanilla traps with their supercharged version based on configurable percent chances.

The vanilla spawn command also supports super-prefixed test names such as superlandmine, superturret, supersoundcannon, supercoil, and similar.

A dedicated spawnsuper console command is included for testing guaranteed supercharged traps.

A spawncategory supertraps console category is included for quickly placing a lineup of the current supercharged traps. The sound cannon in that lineup is spawned deactivated so it does not immediately ruin your day while testing.

[line]

[size=4]Trap Overview (Default config)[/size]

Supercharged landmines have a stronger blast, more severe limb trauma, shrapnel, stronger hearing damage, and a configurable chance for fractures or amputation. Defaults are meant to be dangerous but not automatic character deletion.

Supercharged gunmines and turrets fire heavier rounds with a larger hit radius, custom optional gun sounds, stronger muzzle effects, terrain damage on misses, and extra trauma on hit. Headshots have a configurable survivability floor so they are not always instant death (as I've come to realize that they are somehow faster than the kill command).

Supercharged sound cannons charge more slowly and punish successful hits harder than vanilla. Successful hits use sonarmegaouch.ogg by default, or full-volume sonarouch.ogg when light hit sound mode is enabled. Blocked hits use sonarouch.ogg at low volume and apply only light symptoms.

Supercharged launch pads apply stronger launch force, can throw diagonally, have a longer cooldown, and cap player velocity so they are not simply ceiling-execution machines by default (But you might still get severe brain damage or fracture your skull).

Supercharged spike stabbers can rearm after firing. They keep the vanilla warning-light behavior, retract before becoming dangerous again, and apply meaner wound/bone effects when they hit.

Supercharged bear traps hold the caught limb longer, ramp damage over time, punish struggling, add shrapnel, and damage connected limbs.

Supercharged coils damage instead of helping. They can induce fibrillation progress, apply timed ragdoll, open wounds, and optionally cause brain damage. Defaults are balanced away from instant guaranteed VFib.

[line]

[size=4]Configuration[/size]

The generated config controls the important values.

Useful entries include:

General.Enabled
General.SpawnCommandSuperchargePercent

Spawn Chances.LandMinePercent
Spawn Chances.GunMinePercent
Spawn Chances.TurretPercent
Spawn Chances.SoundCannonPercent
Spawn Chances.LaunchPadPercent
Spawn Chances.SpikeStabberPercent
Spawn Chances.BearTrapPercent
Spawn Chances.CoilPercent

Gun Traps.DamageMultiplier
Gun Traps.ProjectileRadiusWorldUnits
Gun Traps.MissTileDamage
Gun Traps.ProximityFxRange
Gun Traps.HeadshotMinimumBrainHealth

Sound Cannon.UseLightHitSound
Sound Cannon.BrainDamageMultiplier
Sound Cannon.BodyDamageMultiplier
Sound Cannon.WaterMultiplier
Sound Cannon.BlockedHearingLoss
Sound Cannon.BlockedSickness

Launch Pad.ForceMultiplier
Launch Pad.MaxBodyVelocity
Launch Pad.DiagonalLaunchPercent
Launch Pad.CooldownSeconds

Spike Stabber.DamageMultiplier
Spike Stabber.RechargeSeconds
Spike Stabber.RetractSeconds
Spike Stabber.BlinkSeconds

Bear Trap.HoldSeconds
Bear Trap.DamageMultiplier
Bear Trap.TargetBleedAmount
Bear Trap.StruggleMultiplier
Bear Trap.StruggleBoneBreakPercent

Coil.FibrillationProgress
Coil.RagdollSeconds
Coil.OpenWoundPercent
Coil.BrainDamagePercent
Coil.DamageMultiplier

If you delete the config file, BepInEx will regenerate it on next launch with the current defaults.

[line]

[size=4]Custom Assets[/size]

The mod can run without custom assets. Missing custom sprites or sounds fall back to vanilla visuals and sounds where possible.

Optional assets belong in:

[code]BepInEx\plugins\CasualtiesSupercharged\Assets\SuperchargedTraps\[/code]
Supported optional assets include custom PNG sprites, custom OGG sounds, and locale_en.json for tooltip text.

Common optional sound files:

SuperGunmine.ogg
SuperGunturret.ogg
SuperSonarmegaouch.ogg
SuperSonarouch.ogg
SuperSonarcharge.ogg

For compatibility, sonarmegaouch.ogg and sonarouch.ogg are also accepted as aliases for the two super sonar hit sounds.

[line]

[size=4]Console Testing[/size]

Use:

spawnsuper landmine
spawnsuper gunmine
spawnsuper turret
spawnsuper soundcannon
spawnsuper jumppad
spawnsuper spikestabber
spawnsuper beartrap
spawnsuper coil

You can also use the vanilla spawn command with super-prefixed names:

spawn superlandmine
spawn supergunmine
spawn superturret
spawn supersoundcannon
spawn superjumppad
spawn superspikestabber
spawn superbeartrap
spawn supercoil

The normal vanilla spawn command should still spawn normal traps unless General.SpawnCommandSuperchargePercent is above 0 and the roll succeeds.

[line]

[size=4]Mod API[/size]

Other BepInEx mods can reference CasualtiesSupercharged.dll and use SuperchargedTrapsApi.

The API can:

Check whether a trap is supercharged.
Try to read the supercharged trap kind.
Force a vanilla trap GameObject to become supercharged.
Subscribe to a recharged event for traps that become dangerous again after a custom cooldown or rearm cycle.

Supercharged traps remain vanilla trap GameObjects with vanilla components. The API checks the plugin marker component rather than asking other mods to reflect into internal behavior scripts.

[line]

[size=4]Compatibility[/size]

This mod is additive. It does not overwrite game assets.

It may conflict with other mods that heavily replace trap behavior, trap world generation, console spawn commands, or the same Body fields during trap hits.

Mods that only add unrelated items, UI, audio, or quality-of-life behavior are more likely to be fine.
Multiplayer compatibility will only work if the HOST has the mod as they control worldgen (iirc)

The plugin attempts to remain removable by using runtime-only components and vanilla-compatible object state.

If BepInEx HideGameObjectManager is set to false, the plugin creates its own hidden DontDestroyOnLoad manager and attempts to keep it alive even if the visible BepInEx host object is destroyed during scene cleanup.

[line]

[size=4]Save and Uninstall Notes[/size]

The plugin does not intentionally write custom persistent save data.

With the vanilla save system, removing the plugin should leave only normal vanilla player injury state behind, such as bleeding, fractures, shrapnel, brain damage, hearing loss, or other medical effects that already exist in the base game.

Third-party mid-run save mods that serialize entire Unity objects may behave differently. The plugin marks runtime-only components as non-save where possible, but broad object serializers can never be guaranteed safe. (an example would be QoL: Unknown which uses JSON to serialize the world, if the mod is removed between saves all supercharged traps will dissapear.)

For safest uninstalling, finish or abandon the current run first, then remove:

[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\plugins\CasualtiesSupercharged\[/code]
Optional:

[code]<Game Folder>\BepInEx\config\com.carlo.casualtiesunknown.superchargedtraps.cfg[/code]
[line]

[size=4]Troubleshooting[/size]

If supercharged traps do not appear:

[list]
[*]Confirm BepInEx 5 loads.[/*]
[*]Confirm CasualtiesSupercharged.dll is inside BepInEx\plugins.[/*]
[*]Launch once and check that the config file was generated.[/*]
[*]Check that the relevant Spawn Chances config entry is above 0.[/*]
[*]Use spawnsuper to confirm the plugin is active.[/*]
[/list]
If all above fails, try to use "HideGameObjectManager" (BepInEx.cfg) set to true.

If custom sprites or sounds do not appear:
[list]
[*]Confirm the Assets folder is next to the DLL.[/*]
[*]Confirm the files are inside Assets\SuperchargedTraps.[/*]
[*]Confirm the names match the expected filenames.[/*]
[*]Missing assets are not fatal; the mod should fall back to vanilla visuals or sounds.[/*]
[/list]
If a trap feels too lethal:
[list]
[*]Lower the relevant damage multiplier, spawn chance, bleed target, fibrillation progress, water multiplier, or screen effect setting in the config.[/*]
[/list]If the log file gets noisy:

[list]
[*]Check BepInEx\LogOutput.log for repeated warnings or errors from Casualties: Supercharged. Routine status logging is intended to stay quiet.[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=4]Credits[/size]

[list]
[*]Built with BepInEx 5.[/*]
[*]Orsoniks for "sonarmegaouch.ogg".[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=4]Version[/size]

Current workspace version: 1.0.0

This build is experimental and may change as the underlying game and mod hooks are better understood.
Author: yzaCarlos

# 💊 Extra Medicaments — 20 New Medical Items

Adds 20 new, balanced medical items to Casualties: Unknown. Each one has a unique effect — some help with blood pressure, others with infections, pain, or even hearing loss.

| Item | Effect |

| [b]Cardiomagnyl[/b] | Reduces blood thickness and protects against clot formation |

| [b]Bisoprolol[/b] | Lowers blood pressure and slightly helps with arrhythmia |

| [b]Afobazol[/b] | Reduces trauma, but costs a small amount of happiness |

| [b]Suprastin[/b] | Helps against toxicosis and boosts your immune system |

| [b]Trach Tube[/b] | This throat tube supplies oxygen to your blood and helps you breathe. Can only be used on the Head. |

| [b]Hemostatic Sponge[/b] | A first-aid sponge that covers wounds, eases pain, and provides mild disinfection to stop bleeding fast. |

| [b]Stelfrin | [/b]Boosts your blood pressure when it drops too low. Use it with caution. Injected into a vein.[b] |[/b]

| [b]Acetaminophen[/b] | Powerful painkilling action and brings down high temperatures. |

| [b]Validol | [/b]Opens up blood flow, improves happiness, calms the mind, and eases heart flutters and emotional aches. |

| [b]Unknown Pill | [/b]A mysterious pill with unknown effects. Taking it may have unpredictable consequences. Can be used twice. |

Name: i18n Auto Updater
Summary: Automatically downloads and updates localization files from GitHub repositories.
Description:
[url=https://github.com/CNCUMC/i18n-Auto-Updater]GitHub[/url] | [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/447]NexusMods[/url]

[i]Automatically downloads and updates localization files from GitHub repositories.[/i]
[line]
[size=4]Overview[/size]

[b]i18n Auto Updater[/b] is a BepInEx plugin for [b]Casualties Unknown[/b] that automatically checks for and downloads
localization files from GitHub repositories. It supports single file downloads or wildcard mode to fetch all files from
a repository.

[line]
[size=4]Features[/size]

[list]
[*][b]Automatic Updates[/b] — Checks for updates on game startup and at configurable intervals[/*]
[*][b]Single File Mode[/b] — Download a specific localization file[/*]
[*][b]Wildcard Mode[/b] — Download all files from a repository using '[font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]*'[/font][/*]
[*][b]SHA-based Caching[/b] — Only downloads files when content has changed (compares GitHub SHA hashes)[/*]
[*][b]Smart Exclusions[/b] — Automatically skips [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif].github[/font], [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif].gitattributes[/font], [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif].gitignore[/font], [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]README.md[/font],
[font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]TranslationNotes.md[/font][/*]
[*][b]Persistent Cache[/b] — Stores file SHA hashes in a JSON cache file to avoid redundant downloads[/*]
[*][b]Cancellation Support[/b] — Gracefully stops background tasks when the plugin is destroyed[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4]Installation[/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx]BepInEx 5.x[/url] for Casualties Unknown.[/*]
[*]Download the latest version.[/*]
[*]Place [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]i18nAutoUpdater.dll[/font] in your [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]BepInEx/plugins/i18n Auto Updater/[/font] folder.[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4]Configuration[/size]

Configuration is stored in [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]BepInEx/config/org.cncumc.i18nautoupdater.cfg[/font].

[list]
[*]Repo Path: 'Orsoniks/scavgame-locale' GitHub repository path, format: 'owner/repo'[/*]
[*]File Path: 'zh-CN.json' Path to localization file (relative to repo root), use `*` to download all files[/*]
[*]Branch: 'main' Branch name to download from[/*]
[*]Auto Check On Startup: 'true' Automatically check for updates on game startup[/*]
[*]Check Interval (Hours): '6' Interval between automatic update checks (in hours)[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4]How It Works[/size]

[size=3]Single File Mode[/size]

When [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]File Path[/font] is set to a specific file (e.g., [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]zh-CN.json[/font]):

[list=1]
[*]The plugin queries the GitHub API to get the file's SHA hash[/*]
[*]Compares it with the cached SHA from previous downloads[/*]
[*]If the SHA matches → skips download (logs: [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]Cache analysis: SHA matches cache[/font])[/*]
[*]If the SHA differs → downloads the file and updates the cache[/*]
[/list][size=3]Wildcard Mode[/size]

When [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]File Path[/font] is set to [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]*[/font]:

[list=1]
[*]Fetches the repository's file list from GitHub API[/*]
[*]Filters out excluded files and folders[/*]
[*]For each remaining file:
[list]
[*]Checks if the SHA matches the cache[/*]
[*]Downloads only if changed or new[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*]Logs a summary: [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]Batch update complete: X updated, Y skipped, Z failed[/font][/*]
[/list][size=3]Cache File[/size]

The cache is stored in [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]BepInEx/cache/org.cncumc.i18nautoupdater.json[/font] as a JSON file:

[code]{
"Orsoniks/scavgame-locale/main/zh-CN.json": {
"sha": "a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
"lastUpdate": "2026-07-14T10:00:00Z",
"filePath": "zh-CN.json"
}
}[/code][line]
[size=4]Excluded Files[/size]

The following files and folders are automatically excluded in wildcard mode:

Folder: '.github'         
File: '.gitattributes, '.gitignore', 'README.md', 'translationNotes.md'

[line]
[size=4]Log Messages[/size]

[list]
[*]'i18n Auto Updater loaded!': Plugin initialized[/*]
[*]'Wildcard mode: Fetching file list from repository...': Starting wildcard download[/*]
[*]'Found X files, excluded Y, starting update check...': File list retrieved[/*]
[*]'[Update] path (SHA: old... -> new...)': File updated[/*]
[*]'[New] path': New file downloaded[/*]
[*]'[Error] path: message': Download failed[/*]
[*]'Batch update complete: X updated, Y skipped, Z failed': Wildcard summary[/*]
[*]'Cache analysis: SHA matches cache (hash...), skipping download.': No changes detected[/*]
[*]'Cache analysis: SHA has changed': File changed, downloading[/*]
[*]'Cache analysis: No cache record, downloading for the first time': First download[/*]
[*]'Localization file updated: path, please restart the game!': Update complete[/*]
[*]'Files updated, please restart the game to apply changes!': Multiple files updated[/*]
[/list][line]
[size=4]FAQ[/size]

[b]Q: Where are downloaded files saved?[/b]
A: Files are saved to [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]CasualtiesUnknown_Data/Lang[/font] with their original filename.

[b]Q: How do I clear the cache?[/b]
A: Delete [font=Monaco,Consolas,'Lucida Console','Courier New',serif]BepInEx/cache/org.cncumc.i18nautoupdater.json[/font]. The plugin will re-download all files on the next check.

[b]Q: Can I use this with private repositories?[/b]
A: No, this plugin only supports public repositories via the GitHub API.

[b]Q: What happens if GitHub API is rate-limited?[/b]
A: The plugin will log an error and retry at the next scheduled check interval.

Name: NeurotraumaModik
Summary: Adds Neurotrauma-style complications to Casualties Unknown — frostbite, necrosis, pneumothorax, organ transplants, surgery tools, moodle icons & host-authoritative MP.
Description:
[center][b][size=5]NeurotraumaModik[/size][/b][/center]
[center][i][i]Barotrauma Neurotrauma-style medical realism for Casualties Unknown[/i][/i][/center]

[center][b]Version[/b] 2.3.2 · [b]Author[/b] Staili · [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/440]Nexus[/url][/center]

[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
A BepInEx plugin — adaptation of [b]Neurotrauma[/b] (Barotrauma) for [b]Casualties Unknown[/b], built on [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/341][b]CUCoreLib[/b][/url].
[b]Multiplayer sync is optional[/b]: with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/67][b]Casualties Together (KrokMP)[/b][/url] afflictions sync in lobby; [b]without KrokMP the mod runs fully in single-player[/b].

One DLL (icons embedded) + a small [b]Content\Sound[/b] folder — no game file edits. Drop into [b]BepInEx\plugins\[/b].

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Afflictions[/b] — complications with icons and localized cure hints, tied to vanilla vitals (infection, cold, chest trauma, radiation, mood, alcohol, etc.). Includes fever ([b]fever[/b]), seizures ([b]seizure[/b] — aim penalty; rare control glitches above 30%), staged liver icons ([b]pechen_warning[/b] → [b]pechen_warning2[/b] → [b]pechen_dead[/b]), kidney/lung tiers, UNI-HEALTH chip faults, parasites, cuts/sutures, and more.[/*]
[*][b]Wound-view UI[/b] — per-limb icons on the body schematic; docked panel shows severity, category, treatments, and your blood type.[/*]
[*][b]Vanilla moodle bar[/b] — active mod afflictions in the bottom status strip (toggle: [b]ShowModMoodles[/b]).[/*]
[*][b]Surgery[/b] — not one-click: scalpel incision ([b]porez1[/b]) → retractor widen ([b]porez3[/b]) → internals; scissors extract foreign bodies; close with vanilla [b]medicalsuture[/b]. Tools: [b]nt_scalpel[/b], [b]nt_bonesaw[/b], [b]nt_retractor[/b], [b]nt_scissors[/b]. Transplants use one vanilla [b]internalorgans[/b] (≥40%) per organ (heart / lungs / kidneys / liver). Anesthesia via O2 condenser + serum.[/*]
[*][b]Parasites[/b] — after ~6 minutes of untreated [b]porez4/5_foreign[/b], random 1–5 parasites burrow ([b]parazite[/b] moodle at 100%). Extract with hands or vanilla tweezers (minigame). In MP (with KrokMP) peers can pull together. [b]nt_antiparasite[/b] is a [b]3-dose[/b] prophylaxis vial (~6 min) — does [b]not[/b] remove already burrowed parasites. Toggle: [b]EnableParasites[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Blood type (ABO+Rh)[/b] — random at spawn; shown on the panel and yellow blood-bag tooltips; persists across layers / [b]save.sv[/b]. Wrong typed transfusion → ~3 min high BP (~160) and HR 120. Craft: [b]bloodbag[/b] + 20 mL [b]alienblood[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Per-limb[/b] wounds / frostbite / chronic pain / parasites — tracked per extremity; synced in MP when KrokMP is present.[/*]
[*][b]Phantom effects[/b] — client-side spiders, vignette, whispers; psychosis >30 auditory flashbacks ([b]HallucinationVisuals[/b]).[/*]
[*][b]Multiplayer (optional)[/b] — with KrokMP: host-authoritative state, host symptom mask, heal allies in UNI-HEALTH, shared parasite minigame. Players without this mod may still join the lobby.[/*]
[*][b]Save persistence[/b] — mod status, blood type, parasite counts, and foreign-wound age in a [b]neurotrauma[/b] block inside [b]save.sv[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Crafting & loot[/b] — Medicine recipes; loot toggle [b]AddToLootPool[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Prosthetics compat[/b] — optional [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/scavprototype/mods/40]Herobrine's Prosthetics[/url]: prosthetic limbs skip per-limb necrosis/tetanus/frostbite/chronic pain.[/*]
[*][b]Debug console[/b] — [b]nt_list[/b], [b]nt_add[/b], [b]nt_set[/b], [b]nt_clear[/b], [b]nt_diag[/b], [b]nt_limbs[/b], [b]nt_bloodtype[/b] (+ autofill; names with spaces OK). MP needs [b]sv_cheats[/b].[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Items[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]nt_scalpel[/b] — surgery: incision, necrosis debridement[/*]
[*][b]nt_bonesaw[/b] — amputation & organ transplant[/*]
[*][b]nt_retractor[/b] — widen wound, pleural drain, internals[/*]
[*][b]nt_scissors[/b] — foreign-body extract; eject condenser serum[/*]
[*][b]nt_antiparasite[/b] — 3 doses; prophylaxis (~6 min); mild liver/sepsis help — does not extract burrowed parasites[/*]
[*][b]nt_serum_sleep[/b] — anesthetic charge for the condenser[/*]
[*][b]nt_o2_condenser[/b] — empty = O₂ / clear hyperventilation; with serum = anesthesia[/*]
[*][b]nt_important_chip[/b] — replace a failing UNI-HEALTH board (craft: circuit board ≥90% + string×2)[/*]
[*][b]nt_bloodtype_op[/b] … [b]nt_bloodtype_abm[/b] — typed yellow blood packs[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx/releases/download/v5.4.23.5/BepInEx_win_x64_5.4.23.5.zip]BepInEx 5.4.23.5 (win_x64)[/url] — extract next to [b]CasualtiesUnknown.exe[/b][/*]

For MP sync, everyone with Neurotrauma should use the [b]same plugin + CUCoreLib[/b] (and KrokMP) version.
